editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Let \(p\) and \(q\) be square free relatively prime integers so that \(p = 3 \bmod 16\), \(q = 11 \bmod 16\) and \(p \cdot q = 1 \bmod 32\). Let \(G\) be the graph whose vertices are points in \(Q (\sqrt p, \sqrt q)^2\) with an edge between two of them if their Euclidean distance is 1. We show that this graph has an additive 4-coloring. Specifically, we prove the existence of a group homomorphism \(v : \Sigma = \{\sum^n_1 \xi_j : \xi_j \in Q (\sqrt p, \sqrt q,i)\), \(\xi_j \cdot \overline \xi_j = 1\} \to {Z \over (4)}\) so that \(v (\xi) \neq 0\) whenever \(\xi\) is a complex number in \(Q (\sqrt p, \sqrt q,i)\) of complex norm 1. Since the graph \(Q (\sqrt 3, \sqrt {11})^2\) contains finite graphs which require four colors, it follows that the chromatic number of this graph is 4.
